messages:
kevin: heads up — Support ticket 5231 from partner-acme: intermittent 401s on our /v1/hooks/verify endpoint. They see ~1-3% of requests failing with "invalid_signature" and some with "token_expired". Happening since yesterday afternoon. sample header they provided: Authorization: Bearer <jwt>

ana: can you paste the raw error from our logs? also which region/customer?

kevin: logs: `auth.verify: jwt verification failed: kid not found in local JWKS cache` and later `auth.verify: token expired (exp < now)`. Region: us-west-2, partner-acme org id. Attached curl they ran to our endpoint.

maria: interesting — kid not found usually means JWKS rotated on their side and our cache didn't pick it up. but token_expired is a separate thing (clock skew). could be two different issues.

sam: @oncall I'm going to try reproducing quickly. any chance partner shares their jwks_uri?

kevin: yes. jwks_uri: https://partners.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json — they also said they send Cache-Control: max-age=86400 on that endpoint.

ana: ugh. 24h max-age is aggressive for key rotation. If they rotated keys and didn't set short TTL, our cache would keep old keys for a day. but we should also have a fallback: if kid not found, re-fetch JWKS and retry once. do we do that?

sam: current runtime caches JWKS per-issuer for 1h by default, but we honor cache-control if present. however the cache is primarily in-process and there's a short-circuit to avoid thundering herd; iirc we only re-fetch after TTL expiry. so kid-not-found won't trigger immediate refetch — that's our bug.

maria: that explains the intermittent nature: if a request hits a different instance with fresh cache, it passes; otherwise 401. clock skew explains the token_expired entries — some partner hosts have NTP drift. How big is the skew?

kevin: partner sent sample JWTs. I decoded one: exp = 1700000000, iat = 1699999400. Server's timestamp at failure was 1700000365 -> iat is in the past but exp < now? weird. Looking at one failure trace, their system clock was ~7 minutes behind our server. that would make token appear not-yet-valid or expired depending on direction.

ana: ok actionable list then: 1) fix JWKS flow to re-fetch on kid-not-found and retry verification once. 2) relax allowed clock skew leeway to 120s by default or make configurable per-issuer. 3) add observability metrics for JWKS misses and clock-skew-induced rejects.

sam: repro steps I used locally:
```bash
# fetch jwks, save
curl -sS https://partners.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json -o acme_jwks.json
# issue a jwt using old key (simulate rotated) then verify 
python -c "from jose import jwt; print('TODO: create token with kid X')"
# run verify against our auth lib with cache mocked to stale JWKS
```

kevin: I also tried forcing clock skew in our verifier with pyjwt by setting leeway=0 and then leeway=120, behavior matches: with 0 we see expirations, 120 fixes the tests.

maria: small nit — we should be careful increasing leeway globally. better to allow per-issuer configuration or have a default 60-120s. some issuers may intentionally set tight windows.

ana: agreed. propose default 120s and allow override via issuer config in the console/tenant settings (for Dedicated/Private). For hosted customers we can give a tenant-level toggle and breakglass.

oncall: I opened incident P-2026 and pinned: "JWT verification — handle JWKS rotation + clock skew". assigning to eng-runtime and eng-security.

kevin: PR draft I started (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987 — changes: on kid-not-found -> async fetch JWKS, update cache, retry verify once. add metric `jwks_refetch_on_kid_missing_total`. also expose `allowed_clock_skew_seconds` with default 120.

sam: test matrix to cover: 
- normal verification (no refetch)
- kid-rotated: initial cache stale -> refetch -> success
- kid-rotated: refetch fails (404/500) -> surface 401 and increment metric
- clock skew: +/- 0/60/120s

maria: we should also update docs for integrators: recommend they set short jwks cache-control (max-age <= 300) or set up cache-invalidation hooks. provide example curl to rotate keys and best practices.

kevin: I drafted a short notice to partner-acme support: "we're deploying a fix that will allow immediate JWKS refresh when a kid is missing and add a small clock skew leeway. In the meantime please ensure your JWKS endpoint sends short cache TTL or notify us via support when you rotate keys." want me to send?

ana: yes, send and mention they should check NTP on their servers. include repro curl commands and suggest retesting after we deploy.

maria: follow-up ops: schedule rollout to canary (10% traffic) with monitoring on new metric and auth 5xx/401 rates. rollback flag if error rate increases.

kevin: timeline: I'll finish PR today, tests tomorrow, canary deploy Wed. I'll update incident with links.

sam: thanks. quick snippet to reproduce kid-not-found locally for QA:
```python
# patch in-memory jwks cache with only key A, then verify token signed with key B
# run verifier -> expect kid-not-found -> trigger refetch -> verify succeeds if remote jwks has B
```

incident-bot: Incident P-2026 created by oncall. Severity: P2. Linked PR: runtime#987.

ana: summary for thread: root cause = aggressive partner JWKS TTL + runtime didn't re-fetch on kid-missing; separate issue = partner clock skew causing exp/nbf failures. fixes = immediate refetch-on-kid-missing + configurable clock-skew leeway + metrics + docs + partner notification. action owners: kevin (PR + partner comms), sam (tests + canary), maria (docs + metrics), oncall (rollout). ETA canary Wed.

kevin: tagging this for follow-up in postmortems channel once resolved. :thumbsup:
